title: Present Simple
description: Habits, ownership, and facts that stay true in standups and docs.

lessons.title: Form
lessons.description: Build habits and facts. Cue: every / usually / still.
lessons.usage: Goal: report routines, owners, and stable facts — not live WIP.
exampleSentences: I ship small fixes every morning.
We review pull requests on Fridays.
tips: he/she/it takes -s; don't/doesn't + base (not doesn't goes).
WIP in this standup uses Present Continuous, not Simple.

lessons.title: Use
lessons.description: Simple = habit/fact. Continuous = live now.
lessons.usage: Goal: pick Simple vs Continuous from cues (every / usually vs right now).
exampleSentences: She reviews pull requests every Friday.
I am shipping this hotfix now.
tips: A schedule or owner stays Simple even if you mention today.
Do not use Simple for a ticket you are working this standup.

lessons.title: Apply
lessons.description: Policy, SLA, and stative verbs stay Simple.
lessons.usage: Goal: keep contracts, SLAs, and statives (own, need, mean) in Simple.
exampleSentences: This change requires a dual-write window.
The worker owns the outbox table.
The API returns 409 on duplicate keys.
It means the cache is the source of truth.
tips: Never mark is owning / is needing / is meaning as correct.
Written policy uses Simple, not a live Continuous snapshot.

exercises.prompt: Choose the negative: He ___ on-call on Mondays.

payload.template: The gateway ___ unsigned tokens.

Cue: right now. I ___ the hotfix.

I ___ this one now.

exercises.prompt: It ___ the cache is the source of truth.

payload.template: This change ___ a dual-write window.
The API ___ 409 on duplicate keys.

title: Present Continuous
description: Live WIP, current incidents, and work in progress this standup.

lessons.title: Form
lessons.description: am/is/are + V-ing for work happening now.
lessons.usage: Goal: say what is in progress in this standup or incident.
exampleSentences: I am debugging the auth timeout.
We are rolling back the bad deploy.
She is reviewing the migration now.
The worker is retrying failed jobs.
They aren't merging until tests pass.
tips: Use be + V-ing, not I debugging.
Statives (own, know, need) stay Simple.

lessons.title: Use
lessons.description: Now / at the moment vs habits and owners.
lessons.usage: Goal: use Continuous for this-cycle WIP; keep owners and schedules Simple.
exampleSentences: I am pairing on the flaky test right now.
At the moment we are seeing 5xx on checkout.
I usually handle alerts, but I am shadowing today.
He is rewriting the retry loop this morning.
tips: right now / at the moment / this morning (WIP) → Continuous.
usually / owns / every → Simple.

lessons.title: Apply
lessons.description: Incident English: current impact without over-claiming.
lessons.usage: Goal: report live impact and actions; keep hypotheses hedged.
exampleSentences: We are mitigating checkout 5xx with a feature flag.
I am collecting traces before we page secondary.
Engineering is not changing the schema in this window.
Customers are still hitting the stale cache.
This service owns retries; we are only adding metrics.
tips: Live impact → Continuous; ownership → Simple.
Avoid is meaning / is needing in incident notes.

title: Past Simple
description: Finished actions: shipped, merged, rolled back, closed.

lessons.title: Form
lessons.description: V-ed / irregular past. Cue: yesterday / last night / at 14:00.
lessons.usage: Goal: report finished work with a finished time.
exampleSentences: Did you ship the flag change?
tips: didn't + base (not didn't merged).
Finished clock time → Past Simple, not Present Perfect.

lessons.title: Use
lessons.description: Finished time vs result that still matters.
lessons.usage: Goal: Past Simple for finished stamps; Present Perfect for open results.
exampleSentences: I shipped the patch last night.
The worker failed twice, then recovered.
I have not seen new errors since then.
tips: yesterday / last night / at 09:12 → Past Simple.
already / yet / so far / since → Present Perfect.

lessons.title: Apply
lessons.description: Incident timeline: stamp finished actions clearly.
lessons.usage: Goal: write a clean past timeline for tickets and incident notes.

I reverted the migration after the lock timeout.
Pager fired; she acknowledged in two minutes.
We did not declare an incident because impact stayed local.
The dual-write window closed on Tuesday.
tips: Keep one finished verb per stamped action.
Do not mix have + yesterday in the same clause.

title: Past Continuous
description: Background work in progress when another event happened.

lessons.title: Form
lessons.description: was/were + V-ing for background past WIP.
lessons.usage: Goal: say what was in progress at a past moment.
exampleSentences: I was debugging when the page fired.
We were deploying when latency spiked.
She was reviewing the diff at 16:00.
Were you still pairing at that point?
tips: was/were + V-ing, not was debug.
A finished interrupt uses Past Simple.

lessons.title: Use
lessons.description: Background vs finished interrupt.
lessons.usage: Goal: Continuous for the scene; Simple for the event that cut in.
exampleSentences: I was writing the RFC when Slack lit up.
While we were failing over, checkout stayed up.
He merged after we were already rolling back.
The job was retrying when the lock expired.
I finished the notes after the call ended.
tips: when/while + Continuous = background.
The interrupting event is usually Past Simple.

lessons.title: Apply
lessons.description: Incident narrative: what was running when impact started.
lessons.usage: Goal: set the scene of an incident without mixing Perfect clocks.
exampleSentences: We were draining connections when the proxy restarted.
Customers were checking out while we failed over.
I was not changing prod config during that window.
The canary was soaking when error rate jumped.
Two writers were active when the unique index landed.
tips: Use Continuous for overlapping work, Simple for the trigger.
Do not stamp was + V-ing with already/yet.

title: Present Perfect
description: Results that still matter: already, yet, so far, since.

lessons.title: Form
lessons.description: have/has + past participle. Cue: already / yet / so far.
lessons.usage: Goal: report an open result without a finished clock stamp.
exampleSentences: We have not seen new 5xx yet.
She has already updated the runbook.
So far we have recovered checkout.
tips: have/has + participle, not have + yesterday.
yet usually sits in negatives and questions.

lessons.title: Use
lessons.description: Perfect result vs Past Simple stamp.
lessons.usage: Goal: already/yet/since/so far → Perfect; yesterday/at 14:00 → Past Simple.
exampleSentences: I have already shipped the flag.
She has not approved the RFC yet.
Errors have dropped since the revert.
tips: since + starting point keeps Present Perfect.
A clock time in the same clause usually forces Past Simple.

lessons.title: Apply
lessons.description: Status that is still true for clients and tickets.
lessons.usage: Goal: give current status with Perfect; stamp history with Simple.
exampleSentences: We have restored checkout; monitoring is still open.
We have not confirmed a root cause yet.
I have added the missing index since the review.
Pages have stayed quiet for 40 minutes.
tips: Client updates prefer have/has for unfinished investigation.
Do not write have restored at 12:40 in one clause.

title: Future Forms
description: will vs going to for decisions, plans, and client promises.

lessons.title: Form
lessons.description: will + V and be going to + V.
lessons.usage: Goal: form decisions (will) and plans already decided (going to).

forms.affirmative: will + V  ·  am/is/are going to + V
forms.negative: won't + V  ·  am/is/are not going to + V
forms.question: Will + subject + V?  ·  Be + going to + V?

exampleSentences: I will pair with you after this call.
We are going to roll forward at 18:00.
She won't merge until CI is green.
We are going to share an ETA today.
Will you take the on-call swap?
tips: will + base, not will to / will merging.
going to + base, not going to + V-ing.

lessons.title: Use
lessons.description: will = decision now; going to = plan already set.
lessons.usage: Goal: choose will for instant offers/decisions and going to for scheduled plans.

forms.affirmative: will + V  ·  am/is/are going to + V
forms.negative: won't + V  ·  am/is/are not going to + V
forms.question: Will + subject + V?  ·  Be + going to + V?

We are going to fail over at 21:00 as planned.
I will address the comments this afternoon.
We are going to send a written update by 16:00.
If CI stays red, we will slip the train.
tips: Okay, I will... is a decision in the meeting.
as planned / at 21:00 on the calendar → going to.

lessons.title: Apply
lessons.description: Client promises vs internal plans.
lessons.usage: Goal: sound reliable: going to for committed plans, will for next-step decisions.

forms.affirmative: will + V  ·  am/is/are going to + V

title: Progress & Earlier Past
description: Optional: Present Perfect Continuous, Past Perfect, and Past Perfect Continuous.

lessons.title: Form
lessons.description: have been + V-ing and had + V-ed for earlier past.
lessons.usage: Goal: introduce duration up to now (have been) and the earlier of two pasts (had).

forms.affirmative: have/has been + V-ing  ·  had + past participle
forms.negative: haven't/hasn't been + V-ing  ·  hadn't + past participle
forms.question: Have/Has + subject + been + V-ing?  ·  Had + subject + V-ed?

exampleSentences: I have been chasing the flaky test all morning.
We had already failed over before the page storm.
She has been rewriting the retry loop since Monday.
The job had died before the lock expired.
Had you seen the 5xx before we reverted?
tips: have been + V-ing for unfinished duration; had + participle for earlier past.
These forms are optional — Core Tenses already cover daily status.

lessons.title: Use
lessons.description: Duration vs earlier cause in incident notes.
lessons.usage: Goal: have been for ongoing effort; had for the cause that happened first.

forms.affirmative: have/has been + V-ing  ·  had + past participle
forms.negative: haven't/hasn't been + V-ing  ·  hadn't + past participle
forms.question: Have/Has + subject + been + V-ing?  ·  Had + subject + V-ed?

exampleSentences: We have been soaking the canary for 40 minutes.
The cache had gone stale before checkout failed.
I have been blocked on access since standup.
He had opened the RFC before we found the lock.
We had not reproduced it until this morning.
tips: If both events are finished, the earlier one often takes had.
Do not use had when the result is still true now — use have/has.

lessons.title: Apply
lessons.description: Past Perfect Continuous for long background before a past event.
lessons.usage: Goal: had been + V-ing when a long past effort was running before a cutoff.

We had been draining traffic before the proxy restart.
I had not been watching canary when the page fired.
She had been holding the lock when the timeout hit.
Two writers had been active before the unique index landed.
tips: had been + V-ing = long background that stopped (or was cut) in the past.
Skip this form in daily standups unless the timeline is genuinely nested.

title: Clear Sentence Building
description: Articles, connectors, and verb patterns that keep tickets readable.

lessons.title: Form
lessons.description: a/an/the and common verb patterns (to vs -ing).
lessons.usage: Goal: pick a/an/the and the right verb pattern in a short ticket line.

forms.affirmative: a/an + first mention · the + known item · V + to/-ing
forms.negative: no article with general mass nouns (latency, traffic)
forms.question: Need to + V?  Avoid + V-ing?

exampleSentences: I added an index on the payments table.
The latency is still high on checkout.
We need to revert the flag.
Avoid holding the lock in the request path.
tips: a/an = first mention; the = this known thing.
need to + base; avoid + V-ing (not avoid to).

lessons.title: Use
lessons.description: Connectors: because, so, however in ticket English.
lessons.usage: Goal: join cause, result, and contrast without a run-on.

forms.affirmative: because + cause · so + result · however + contrast
forms.negative: Do not stack however so because in one breath.
forms.question: Why? Because… / So what is next?

exampleSentences: Checkout failed because the cache was stale.
CI is red, so I will not merge.
The query is correct; however, it still tablescans.
We rolled back so customers could check out.
Impact is local. However, we are still investigating.
tips: because = why; so = therefore; however = contrast.
however usually needs a full stop or semicolon, not a comma splice.

lessons.title: Apply
lessons.description: Tight RFC English: one idea, one connector, no fluff.
lessons.usage: Goal: write a ticket sentence that a reviewer can scan.

forms.question: What does this mean for checkout?

The index is missing, which means checkout tablescans.
Latency is unmeasured, so this is still a hypothesis.
Please avoid blocking the writer; use a queue instead.
The workaround holds; however, we still owe a patch.
tips: which means + full clause.
Prefer avoid + V-ing; "Please avoid to block" is a common mistake (shown as Do not).

title: Passive & Relative Structures
description: Passives and relative clauses for tickets, RFCs, and incident notes.

lessons.title: Form
lessons.description: be + past participle; who/which/that for extra info.
lessons.usage: Goal: form a short passive and a relative clause.

forms.question: Was the flag reverted?  The job that failed…

exampleSentences: The job that failed is being retried.

tips: Passive = be + participle (was reverted, not was revert).
who = people; which/that = things.

lessons.title: Use
lessons.description: When passive hides the actor; when relative keeps the ticket tight.
lessons.usage: Goal: use passive for the action; name the owner only when it matters.

forms.affirmative: X was deployed.  The service that owns retries…
forms.negative: Do not write was been deployed.
forms.question: Who owns it? vs What was deployed?

exampleSentences: Checkout was degraded for twelve minutes.
The patch that landed last night is still soaking.
I reverted the flag — I own that call.
The worker which writes the outbox was restarted.
A workaround was published in the status page.
tips: Passive is fine when the actor is obvious or unknown.
Switch to active when you need a named owner.

title: Requests, Questions & Modals
description: can/could/should/must for asks, advice, and incident gates.

lessons.title: Form
lessons.description: Modal + base verb. Cue: Can you / Could you / Should we.
lessons.usage: Goal: form a polite ask and a clear obligation.
exampleSentences: Could you review this RFC today?
Can you take the on-call swap?
We should add a rollback note.
We must not ship schema changes in this freeze.
I can't merge until CI is green.
tips: Modal + base (could you review, not could you to review).
must not / can't — not must to / should to.

lessons.title: Use
lessons.description: could = polite; should = advice; must = hard gate.
lessons.usage: Goal: match modal strength to standup, review, and incident.

forms.affirmative: could you…  ·  we should…  ·  we must…
forms.negative: mustn't for policy; shouldn't for advice
forms.question: Should we page secondary?

exampleSentences: Could you leave a comment on the lock risk?
We should slip the train if CI stays red.
We must page secondary on P0.
You might be blocked on access — can you confirm?
Could we move the call to 16:00?
tips: could you is softer than can you for reviews.
must is for policy and P0, not taste.

lessons.title: Apply
lessons.description: Tone: requests vs orders in incidents and client threads.
lessons.usage: Goal: stay firm on safety, polite on asks, hedged on guesses.

forms.affirmative: Could you…  ·  We should…  ·  This might be…
forms.negative: Avoid You must when a could you would land the review.
forms.question: Can you confirm? vs Must we declare?

exampleSentences: This might be a cache issue — can you confirm on staging?
Could you share the failing request id?
We must keep the flag off until error rate drops.
You should add a metric before we ship this.
I can take the extra on-call hour.
tips: might/may for unmeasured hypotheses.
must for safety gates; could you for information asks.

title: Conditions, Reporting & Tone
description: If-clauses, reported speech, and hedging for tickets and clients.

lessons.title: Form
lessons.description: If + present, will… and told/said reporting.
lessons.usage: Goal: form a real condition and a short reported line.

forms.affirmative: If + present, will + V  ·  X told me (that) + clause
forms.negative: If CI isn't green, we won't merge.
forms.question: What did she say? She said the flag was off.

exampleSentences: If CI stays green, we will ship today.
She told me the flag was already off.
He said the tests were flaky.
If we don't get a request id, we cannot reproduce.
I told the channel we were rolling back.
tips: If + present, will + base (not if will).
told + person; said + clause (not said me).

lessons.title: Use
lessons.description: Real vs hypothetical; backshift in reports.
lessons.usage: Goal: choose if/will vs if/would; backshift when the report is later.

forms.affirmative: If we ship now, we will…  ·  If we shipped now, we would…
forms.negative: She said she was blocked (not she is, if the report is later).
forms.question: What would we do if CI stayed red?

exampleSentences: If we merge now, we will miss the freeze.
If we merged without dual-write, we would lose rollback.
She said she was blocked on access.
They asked if we could move the window.
He told me the tests had failed twice.
tips: Real next step → if + present, will.
Hypothetical / advice → if + past, would.

lessons.title: Apply
lessons.description: Client tone: hedge, report, and condition without over-promising.
lessons.usage: Goal: report status with if/will, hedges, and clear owners.

forms.affirmative: If X holds, we will…  ·  They asked us to…  ·  This seems…
forms.negative: Avoid We will have fixed it yesterday in a client mail.
forms.question: Could you confirm if the workaround still holds?

exampleSentences: If the workaround holds, we will keep it overnight.
They asked us to confirm the request id.
This seems like a cache issue, not a code change.
He said the rollback had already been tested.
We would delay cutover if error rate stays high.
tips: seems/appears/might keep you honest when RCA is open.
would + delay for a conditional plan, not a fake promise.
